title: eval-harness: integrate prompt-regression metrics into CI hooks
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Add CI hook that runs eval-harness prompt-set regression checks and emits per-prompt metrics and annotations. This enables early detection of quality regressions against a pinned prompt set.
description: Context: Engineering and product teams have requested stronger CI-level quality gating for prompt-set regressions (ENG-2147). This PR wires upstream eval metrics into our GitHub Actions CI so that every PR touching model prompts, evals, or serving paths runs the eval-harness regression checks. Motivation: Previously we ran eval-harness on a cadence and relied on post-merge alerts. That delayed detection and caused a production regression last quarter. This change ensures fast feedback to authors with actionable per-prompt metrics and inline annotations. What this PR does (summary): - Adds a new GitHub Actions hook job (ci/eval-regression-check.yml) that runs a lightweight eval-harness job against the repository's canonical prompt sets and a small smoke model runner. - Integrates core eval metrics (accuracy/EM, ROUGE-L, embedding-similarity, and our custom semantic fallback score) into the CI runner and makes thresholds configurable via .eval/config/ci_thresholds.yaml. - Adds an annotations & SARIF-style results exporter so failures show up on the PR with per-prompt diffs and suggested rollback candidates. - Wires results into GitHub checks API and our internal Linear alerting (ENG-2199) for flaky detection. - Adds docs and a README describing how to tune thresholds and how to run the check locally. Commit summary: see commits field. Changed areas: list of high-level files changed below. Testing/CI: initial runs hit a transient model-serving timeout; retries and small timeouts were added. Final green CI run included unit tests + integration smoke run. Backwards compatibility: default thresholds are conservative; no blocking changes to production behavior.

Threshold tuning: docs/eval/ci_gating.md has recommended defaults and a short recipe for teams
Performance: eval job is intentionally small (subset of prompt-set) to keep CI time < 10 minutes; full evals remain on cadence jobs.
post_merge_actions: Added Linear automation: failing CI eval creates a linked Linear ticket (ENG-2199) for triage
Monitoring: added Datadog dashboard fragment for CI eval success rate
Follow-up: track adoption via weekly report for 2 weeks
how_to_revert: Reverting is a single-commit revert of the squash merge. The GitHub action file is namespaced under eval-harness/ci/actions so removal is straightforward. For immediate suppression, set .eval/config/ci_enabled: false in repo root.
user_visible_changes: PR annotations with per-prompt metric breakdown, a new CI check 'eval-regression-check', and docs describing thresholds/tuning.
additional_context: This PR is part of a broader effort to reduce production regressions by providing faster feedback loops for prompt and eval changes. Related PRs: ENG-2147 epic and SUP-987 incident follow-up.
security_considerations: No new secrets added. The CI runner uses existing service account tokens and the GH checks API. SARIF export does not contain PII and is limited to failure diffs and metric numbers.
backwards_compatibility: Conservative default thresholds mean no existing CI will start failing unexpectedly. Teams can tighten thresholds when ready.
tests_added: tests/eval/test_ci_integration.py covers runner retry logic and sarif exporter behavior; unit tests added for summary metric aggregation.
notes: Drafted with input from infra and product; staged for rollout to other repos after 2 weeks of stability.
